title: Balcones Plan, City Bonds, & Services
summary:
*   City leaders prioritized a payment for the Balcones Canyonland Conservation Plan.
*   Discussions focused on a crucial 1992-93 bond sale structure intended to fund city operations and infrastructure projects.
*   Public interest groups, including Austin Interfaith, provided input on the city's financial plans.
*   Department heads from Public Works, Emergency Services, Police, and others presented their capital budget needs for funding through the proposed bond sale.

Mayor Todd called to order the special called meeting of the Council, noting the absence
of Councilmember Epstein. He announced the purpose of the meeting was to have a budget
worksession and listen to reports from the departments listed on the agenda. Mayor Todd
said first of all he wanted to discuss the Balcones Canyonland Conservation Plan payment.
City Manager Barnett discussed the proposed bond sale structure for 1992-93, as well as
Betty Dunkerley, Finance Director and Bill Stockton, Director of Public Works and
Transportation. There was discussion on flood control, parks and various other concerns.
Mrs. Dunkerley said the bond sale should be before September 22, 1992 and then Council can
set the tax rate. Joe Higgs and Robert Martinez of Austin Interfaith made comments.
The departments listed below were not called on to make their presentations, but only to
answer questions of Mayor and Council as it pertained to the bond sale. The meeting was
adjourned at 3:13. Budget Worksession
